title: runtime: add KV allocator fragmentation counters + export hooks
author: Samir Qureshi
description: Context: We’ve been chasing burst-driven p95/p99 spikes that correlate with KV arena churn and suspected allocator fragmentation. Before we can tune compaction/eviction, we need allocator-level signals that are (a) cheap, (b) interpretable, and (c) consistent across Hosted/Dedicated. This PR adds a small set of fragmentation/health counters/gauges emitted by the KV cache allocator, and wires them into the standard runtime metrics pipeline so SRE/Perf Canary can build guardrails and dashboards. Metrics added (names are final, definitions in code comments): kv_allocator_free_bytes (gauge): total free bytes in KV arena; kv_allocator_used_bytes (gauge): total used bytes in KV arena; kv_allocator_largest_free_block_bytes (gauge): size of largest contiguous free block (best-effort from free-list); kv_allocator_fragmentation_ratio (gauge): 1 - (largest_free_block_bytes / max(free_bytes, 1)); kv_allocator_alloc_failures_total (counter): allocation failures (pre-OOM); kv_allocator_defrag_slowpath_total (counter): times we had to take slow path to satisfy request due to fragmentation; kv_allocator_free_list_nodes (gauge): number of nodes in free-list (proxy for fragmentation/overhead). Implementation notes: Fragmentation ratio is computed from allocator bookkeeping (no extra scans beyond what we already track for coalescing). Largest-free-block is updated on free/alloc/coalesce operations; we avoid O(n) iteration per request. All updates are behind a lightweight lock already held in the allocator critical section; exported values are read via atomic snapshot to avoid lock contention on scrape. Export is via the existing runtime metrics registry (Prometheus + OTel bridge); names are consistent with our performance standards and use base units (bytes). Dashboard wiring: Adds panels to the internal ‘runtime / kv cache’ dashboard template (initial wiring only; full rollout and alert thresholds are tracked in ENG-4830 and SRE guardrails doc). Adds exemplars tags (model, pool, tier) consistent with other runtime metrics. Testing: Adds unit tests for fragmentation ratio bounds [0,1], largest_free <= free_bytes, and alloc failure counter increments on synthetic out-of-space conditions. Also adds a microbench to ensure metric updates do not regress allocator hot path (>0.5% regression threshold). Rollout: Safe to ship with metrics on by default; no behavior change to allocation decisions. This PR is a prerequisite for compaction worker + scheduler budgeting (ENG-4823/ENG-4824).
commits: runtime/kv: add allocator stats struct + snapshot API
runtime/metrics: register kv_allocator_* gauges/counters in registry
runtime/kv: update free-list bookkeeping to track largest free block cheaply
dashboards: add KV allocator fragmentation panels (template wiring)
tests: add allocator stats invariant tests + microbench for metrics overhead
review_conversation: Allison Grant (review): Metric naming looks good. Please confirm units are bytes (not pages) and ensure fragmentation_ratio is bounded to [0,1] even when free_bytes=0. Also add a short docstring defining the ratio formula; we’ll mirror it in the metrics standard.

Samir Qureshi (author): Yep, all byte units. Added clamp + free_bytes guard (max(free_bytes, 1)). Added docstring on kv_allocator_fragmentation_ratio and largest_free semantics (best-effort, derived from free-list bookkeeping).

Sean Gallagher (review): Two concerns from SRE: (1) scrape-side lock contention; (2) label cardinality. Please avoid reading under allocator lock during Prom scrape. Also keep labels to pool/tier/model only, no request_id/session_id. Can you add a quick microbench for overhead under decode-like churn?

Samir Qureshi (author): Addressed: stats are copied into an atomic snapshot at end of alloc/free; scrape reads do not take allocator lock. Labels are consistent with other runtime metrics (pool/tier/model) and no high-cardinality IDs. Added microbench `kv_allocator_metrics_overhead.cc` and set regression gate to 0.5%.

Logan Wright (review): On OTel bridge: please register gauges as monotonic=false and set explicit unit metadata. Also we should prefer `*_total` suffix for counters only. I see `kv_allocator_alloc_failures_total` is good; `kv_allocator_defrag_slowpath_total` also good.
Samir Qureshi (author): Done. Updated registry to set unit=By for byte gauges and unit=1 for ratios/counters. Verified counters use *_total naming only.
Caleb Johnson (review): Dashboard template change is fine but please keep it minimal (no new alerts here). Also ensure it doesn’t break jsonnet compile in oss pipeline.
Samir Qureshi (author): Kept to panels only; no alerts. Added jsonnet compile target to CI run and confirmed PASS.

Omar El-Sayed (review): For largest_free bookkeeping: are we at risk of stale max when we split blocks? If so, fragmentation_ratio might under-report. That’s okay as long as we document ‘best-effort’. Please add an invariant test that largest_free <= free_bytes and never negative.
Samir Qureshi (author): Agree it’s best-effort; updated comments. Added invariant tests (largest_free <= free_bytes, ratio in [0,1]).
Allison Grant (approval): LGTM after the clamp + unit metadata changes. This will unblock the metrics standard doc update and dashboard work.
Sean Gallagher (approval): Approved. Please post in #eng-sre once this lands so we can start tuning panels/thresholds for canary.
merge_outcome: Merged (squash) by Connor O'Brien into main; will be included in runtime-1.22 train unless reverted.
release_notes:
- Add KV allocator fragmentation/health metrics (free/used bytes, largest free block, fragmentation ratio, slowpath + alloc failure counters) exported via runtime metrics pipeline.
- Add initial dashboard template panels for KV allocator fragmentation (no alerts in this PR).
